## Research

::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}

### Opinion dynamics

I study stochastic models of opinion formation and collective behaviour, with a particular focus on mixing times, metastability, and phase transitions.

My recent work considers nonlinear majority-based dynamics with stubborn agents and the way changes in model parameters produce qualitatively different long-run behaviour.

[Read more →](research.qmd)

:::

::: {.research-card}

### Social learning and multi-armed bandits

I am interested in how agents can use information from their neighbours to learn efficiently in stochastic environments.

My current work studies multi-agent stochastic bandit systems on networks, with the aim of understanding when simple social-learning mechanisms can improve learning speed and reduce regret.

[Read more →](research.qmd)

:::

:::

## About

My research lies at the intersection of probability, stochastic processes, and interacting systems.

I am particularly interested in how simple microscopic interaction rules lead to macroscopic phenomena such as consensus, metastability, phase transitions, and critical slowing. My work uses tools from Markov chains, mean-field approximations, stochastic processes, and asymptotic analysis.

## Research interests

- Markov chains and mixing times
- Stochastic interacting systems
- Opinion dynamics on graphs
- Mean-field limits
- Metastability and hitting times
- Multi-agent learning
- Stochastic multi-armed bandits
